query:
NUL byte in chat message silently truncates the prompt when an mmproj is loaded

**Version:** b9894 (reproduced on a local build; code paths cited below are unchanged at that tag)

## Summary

When llama-server runs with a multimodal projector loaded, every
`/v1/chat/completions` prompt — including pure-text requests — is tokenized
through the mtmd path. `mtmd_input_text` carries the prompt as a bare
NUL-terminated `const char *` with no length field (`tools/mtmd/mtmd.h:68-72`),
so a message containing U+0000 (JSON `"\^@"`, perfectly legal) is **silently
truncated at the NUL**: every later message and the assistant generation prompt
are dropped, no warning is logged, and the request succeeds.

The observable failure is nasty for agent use: a coding agent that reads any
file containing a NUL byte poisons its conversation — the model, prompted with
text ending mid-file, "continues" the file for a few tokens and stops. From the
client's perspective the model just mysteriously stops mid-response
(`finish_reason: stop`).

## Repro

Server (the mmproj ships with the hf repo and loads by default):

```
llama-server --hf-repo unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL --jinja -lv 10
```

Request (note the `\^@` escape, which JSON decodes to a raw NUL):

```
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "stream": false, "max_tokens": 64,
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly the word BANANA and nothing else.\^@ If you can read this sentence, reply APPLE instead."}]
}'
```

With `-lv 10` the response's `__verbose.prompt` shows the rendered prompt ends
exactly at the NUL — no `<|im_end|>`, no `<|im_start|>assistant`:

```
'<|im_start|>user\nReply with exactly the word BANANA and nothing else.'
```

Same request with `--no-mmproj` renders the full prompt (the text-only path
tokenizes with explicit lengths) and the model responds normally. Reproduced
identically with Gemma 4 12B + its mmproj — model-independent.

## Security implications

It is a prompt-integrity/null-byte injection weakness, most closely related to
CWE-158. An embedded NUL can remove:

  - Trusted instructions appended after untrusted content.
  - Closing chat-template delimiters and the assistant generation marker.
  - The remainder of attacker-controlled content.
  - Subsequent conversation messages.

## Suggested fix

Give `mtmd_input_text` an explicit length (and thread it through
`mtmd_tokenize`'s internal splitting), or have the server reject NULs in
message content with a clear error. Silent truncation is the worst outcome.

Eval bug: GGML_ASSERT in ggml_cuda_op_concat with DeepSeek V4 + quantized KV cache (non-contiguous src)

## Name and Version

version: 9939 (92b187c97)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux aarch64

Also reproduced on a build from 7a63fdede. The backtrace below is from a build from early July, where the same condition trips a slightly different assert (see "Problem description").

## Operating systems

Linux

## GGML backends

CUDA, RPC

## Hardware

2x NVIDIA GB10 (aarch64, CUDA 13), 2-node RPC cluster

## Models

DeepSeek-V4-Flash UD-Q4_K_XL (unsloth GGUF)

## Problem description & steps to reproduce

Enabling KV cache quantization (`--cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0`) for DeepSeek V4 crashes the CUDA backend during prompt processing. The same setup with default f16 KV cache works.

Root cause: the DeepSeek V4 graph (#24162, lightning indexer #24231) feeds a **non-contiguous view of the quantized KV cache into `GGML_OP_CONCAT`**. The quantized branch of `ggml_cuda_op_concat` (`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/concat.cu`) only supports contiguous inputs: on current master this trips `GGML_ASSERT(ggml_is_contiguous(src1))`; on the early-July build from the backtrace below the same case reaches the assert inside `concat_cuda` (`GGML_ASSERT(!ggml_is_quantized(src0->type))`, concat.cu:207). The non-quantized branch handles non-contiguous inputs fine.

The CUDA `supports_op` mirrors the contiguity requirement, but the RPC backend's `supports_op` returns `true` unconditionally, so on an RPC worker the op reaches CUDA and aborts. Note the CPU backend has the same assert in `ggml_compute_forward_concat`, so a single-node setup where the scheduler falls back to CPU for this op would likely abort as well (not verified).

Repro:

```bash
# worker:
./build/bin/ggml-rpc-server -H 10.10.10.2 -p 50052

# head:
./build/bin/llama-server \
  --model DeepSeek-V4-Flash-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00005.gguf \
  --rpc 10.10.10.2:50052 \
  --ctx-size 196608 --parallel 2 \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --no-mmap --jinja --port 8080

curl http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"x","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
```

The worker aborts, then the head node fails in `ggml_backend_rpc_buffer_get_tensor`.

I have a working fix on a branch: pack non-contiguous quantized inputs into a contiguous scratch buffer first (a single `cudaMemcpy2DAsync` when the row stride is uniform, otherwise a small packing kernel in one launch), then reuse the existing byte-level concat path; the contiguity asserts are relaxed to `ggml_is_contiguous_rows` (CUDA, `supports_op`, and the CPU backend, whose generic path already handles strided rows). With it:

- `test-backend-ops -o CONCAT` passes 252/252, including new non-contiguous quantized cases, on GB10 (aarch64, CUDA 13) and RTX 4070 (x86_64, CUDA 13.1);
- the setup above survives 33K-token prompts and multi-turn conversations, prompt processing stays at ~194 t/s at 33K ctx (vs f16 KV cache degrading 210 -> 82 t/s past ~18K on the same cluster).

Branch: https://github.com/adubovikov/llama.cpp/tree/cuda-concat-noncont-quant — happy to open a PR if the approach looks acceptable.

Disclosure: this report and the fix branch were prepared with heavy AI (LLM agent) assistance; the debugging, reproduction and benchmarks were run on real hardware as described. Given the project's AI usage policy, feel free to treat the branch as a reference for a maintainer-authored fix instead of a PR.

Misc. bug: GGML_BLAS=ON costs deepseek4 models 25-30% CPU decode / 3x prefill (OpenMP thread war on MLA matmuls)

### Name and Version

c749cb041 (9966), CPU backend, Ubuntu 24.04

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-bench

### Command line

```shell
llama-bench -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00005.gguf -t 32 -p 0 -n 128
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

With `-DGGML_BLAS=ON -DGGML_BLAS_VENDOR=OpenBLAS` (a common build recipe), `deepseek4`
models lose 25-30% decode throughput and ~3x prefill throughput on CPU because the
architecture's dense MLA matmuls route to OpenBLAS, whose OpenMP thread pool fights ggml's
thread pool. `perf` shows ~62% of cycles in libgomp spinlocks + kernel scheduler. Other
MoE architectures (glm-dsa, qwen3moe, gpt-oss) are unaffected — their graphs don't route
to BLAS — which makes this easy to miss and worth either a docs warning or a runtime guard.

## Environment

- build: c749cb041 (9966), Ubuntu 24.04, gcc default
- hardware: AMD EPYC 9V45 (Turin), 32 physical cores /
  1 NUMA node, 512 GB DDR5 (measured triad ~186 GB/s)
- model: unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-GGUF UD-Q4_K_XL (144.44 GiB, reports
  `deepseek4 ?B MXFP4 MoE` — experts are native MXFP4)

## Measurements (llama-bench, -t 32, -p 0 -n 128 / -p 512 -n 0)

| Build | decode tg128 | prefill pp512 |
|---|---|---|
| GGML_BLAS=ON (OpenBLAS) | 7.00 t/s | 23.3 t/s |
| BLAS=ON + `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` | 7.67 t/s | — |
| **GGML_BLAS=OFF (same source, same flags otherwise)** | **9.33 t/s** | **70.4 t/s** |

Control: GLM-5.2 UD-IQ2_M on the same box scores 7.17 tg128 on BOTH builds (glm-dsa never
routes to BLAS).

## perf evidence (BLAS build, decode, 4.7M samples)

```
22.08%  libgomp.so.1.0.0      [.] 0x207ba          (spin)
21.98%  [kernel]              [k] __schedule
11.54%  libggml-cpu.so        [.] ggml_vec_dot_q8_0_q8_0
 7.69%  [kernel]              [k] schedule
 6.43%  libc.so.6             [.] __sched_yield
 5.67%  libggml-cpu.so        [.] ggml_gemv_mxfp4_8x8_q8_0
 4.98%  [kernel]              [k] do_syscall_64
 3.91%  libgomp.so.1.0.0      [.] 0x207c6          (spin)
 3.41%  libopenblasp-r0.3.20  [.] 0x3718a4
```
~62% spin/scheduler, ~19% math. No-BLAS build: math rises to ~43% (vec_dot 28.6%,
gemv_mxfp4 14.1%), remainder is normal OpenMP barrier spin.

## Why env-var pinning doesn't fix it

`OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1` only recovers +10%: the BLAS sections serialize onto one thread
while 31 threads idle-wait (Amdahl), instead of fighting.

One of: (a) docs note that BLAS builds should not be used for deepseek-family CPU
inference; (b) runtime warning when a deepseek-arch model loads on a BLAS backend with
nthreads > 1; (c) don't route these matmuls to BLAS when ggml threading is active.

Misc. bug: llama-quantize fails on DeepSeek-V4 — i32 ffn_gate_tid2eid routing table not excluded from quantization

### Summary

`llama-quantize` fails on DeepSeek-V4 models because the arch's `ffn_gate_tid2eid` tensor is `i32` and isn't excluded from quantization.

### Repro

Convert any DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint (e.g. `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark`) and quantize it:

```bash
python convert_hf_to_gguf.py DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark --outfile v4-q8.gguf --outtype q8_0 --fp8-as-q8
llama-quantize --allow-requantize v4-q8.gguf v4-q4.gguf Q4_K_M
```

Output:

```
[  20/1328] blk.0.ffn_gate_shexp.weight  - [4096, 2048, 1, 1], type = q8_0, converting to q4_K .. size = 8.50 MiB -> 4.50 MiB
[  21/1328] blk.0.ffn_gate_tid2eid.weight - [   6, 129280, 1, 1], type = i32,
llama_model_quantize: failed to quantize: cannot dequantize/convert tensor type i32
```

(thrown at `src/llama-quant.cpp:228`)

### Cause

`blk.N.ffn_gate_tid2eid.weight` (`LLM_TENSOR_FFN_GATE_TID2EID`, declared in `src/llama-arch.cpp` and created in `src/models/deepseek4.cpp` as `{n_expert_used, n_vocab}`) is a **token-id → expert-id index table**, not weights. It's `i32`, so `llama_tensor_quantize_impl` can't convert it.

`llama_tensor_get_type()` in `src/llama-quant.cpp` already excludes the other MoE routing tensor:

```c
quantize &= name.find("ffn_gate_inp.weight") == std::string::npos;
```

but `tid2eid` was never added when DeepSeek-V4 landed (#24162) — understandable, since that work targeted inference.

### Suggested fix

One line, next to the existing router exclusion:

```c
quantize &= name.find("ffn_gate_inp.weight") == std::string::npos;
quantize &= name.find("tid2eid") == std::string::npos;   // DeepSeek-V4: i32 token-id -> expert-id table
```

With this, the tensor is copied through verbatim (2.959 MiB) and quantization completes.

I'm happy to open a PR if that's useful — just say the word (or feel free to take the line directly, it's trivial).

### Notes

- Probably went unnoticed because the public V4 releases already ship quantized (FP8 attention + MXFP4 experts, ~4.4 BPW), so there's little reason to run `llama-quantize` on them. It does matter if you want to push the routed experts below 4 bits.
- Tested on `505b1ed1`, macOS/Metal.

Thanks for the V4 support — it landed fast and the conversion path (incl. `--fp8-as-q8`) worked flawlessly otherwise.

Misc. bug: validation errors on /v1/chat/completions with X-Conversation-Id return 500 bad_function_call instead of 400

## Summary

When a `POST /v1/chat/completions` request carries the `X-Conversation-Id` header (the resumable-stream opt-in from README-dev.md) and the request body fails parameter validation, the server answers `500` with the plain-text body `bad_function_call` instead of the normal `400` JSON error. The same invalid body without the header returns the correct 400.

This hits every user of the bundled webui with a fresh profile, because the webui's default settings send `"backend_sampling": ""` (empty string, invalid type for a boolean field) on every completion, and the webui always sends `X-Conversation-Id`. Result: a first-time or settings-reset webui fails every chat with a generic "Server error (500)" modal.

## Environment

- build: b9978 (0c4fa7a989), Linux x86_64, HIP backend (gfx1151). The bug is in request handling, not in any backend.
- model: reproduced with a Gemma 4 26B-A4B gguf; the request fails before inference, so any model reproduces it.

## Reproduction

Start any `llama-server`, then:

```bash
# without the header: correct 400
curl -sw '\n%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"m"}],"backend_sampling":""}'
# {"error":{"code":400,"message":"Field 'backend_sampling': [json.exception.type_error.302] type must be boolean, but is string","type":"invalid_request_error"}}
# 400

# with the header: 500 bad_function_call
curl -sw '\n%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-Conversation-Id: repro' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"m"}],"backend_sampling":""}'
# bad_function_call
# 500
```

Server log:

```
E srv    operator(): got exception: bad_function_call
```

Any validation failure triggers it; `backend_sampling` as a string is just the one the webui sends.

## Root cause

In `tools/server/server-stream.cpp`:

1. `server_res_spipe::set_req()` attaches the stream pipe (`spipe`) as soon as the header is present, before the request body is parsed.
2. Parameter validation throws, so `server_res_spipe::set_next()` is never called and `next_orig` stays an empty `std::function`.
3. The error path still runs `on_complete()`. Its guard checks `!spipe || next_finished`; both are false, so it calls `next_orig(chunk)` on the empty function, which throws `std::bad_function_call`.
4. The `set_exception_handler` fallback in `tools/server/server-http.cpp` converts that into the plain-text 500, replacing the 400 JSON body that was already prepared.

## Suggested fix (tested)

Extend the guard in `server_res_spipe::on_complete()`:

```cpp
if (!spipe || next_finished || !next_orig) {
    return;
}
```

Rebuilt b9978 with this guard: the repro request now returns the same 400 JSON as the header-less variant, and normal streamed chats with the header keep working. The session created by `create_or_replace()` in `set_req()` may also want eviction on this path, otherwise the failed request leaves a stream session behind.

## Related webui defect

The invalid field comes from the webui itself. In `tools/ui/src/lib/stores/chat.svelte.ts` (`apiOptions` assembly, around line 2392), every sampler field goes through a `hasValue(...)` guard that filters the empty-string placeholder used for unset settings, except this one:

```ts
apiOptions.backend_sampling = currentConfig.backend_sampling;
```

On a fresh profile `currentConfig.backend_sampling` is the `''` placeholder, so the string is sent verbatim and every completion from a default-settings webui fails. Toggling that one switch in the webui settings stores a real boolean and the failure disappears (no other setting is affected; the rest go through the guard), which made this look tied to unrelated settings changes (we first suspected the MCP opt-in). With the server-side 500 fixed the webui at least shows the real 400 message, but the field needs the same guard as its neighbors.

---

convert_hf_to_gguf: KeyError ['num_local_experts', 'num_experts'] converting any non-MoE NomicBert model (CodeRankEmbed, nomic-embed-text-v1)

### What happened

`convert_hf_to_gguf.py` crashes with a `KeyError` when converting **any non-MoE NomicBert model**. Observed concretely with `nomic-ai/CodeRankEmbed` (revision `3c4b60807d71f79b43f3c4363786d9493691f8b1`, `--outtype f16`):

```
INFO:hf-to-gguf:Model architecture: NomicBertModel
INFO:hf-to-gguf:Exporting model...
  File ".../conversion/bert.py", line 372, in modify_tensors
    n_experts = self.find_hparam(["num_local_experts", "num_experts"])
  File ".../conversion/base.py", line 198, in find_hparam
    raise KeyError(f"could not find any of: {keys}")
KeyError: "could not find any of: ['num_local_experts', 'num_experts']"
```

No GGUF is produced; exit code 1. The crash fires on the first tensor.

### Root cause

`NomicBertModel.modify_tensors` (`conversion/bert.py:372`) calls
`self.find_hparam(["num_local_experts", "num_experts"])` **unconditionally** at the top of the method, but the value is only consumed inside the MoE tensor branches (`"mlp.experts.mlp.w1/w2" in name`). Non-MoE NomicBert configs carry neither key (`is_moe` is derived from `moe_every_n_layers`, which is absent → `False`), so `find_hparam` raises on every non-MoE model of this architecture.

This is not specific to CodeRankEmbed:

- `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1` (the canonical non-MoE NomicBert) also has no `num_experts`/`num_local_experts` in its `config.json` — only `nomic-embed-text-v2-moe` carries them (`num_experts: 8`, `moe_every_n_layers: 2`).
- Probing CodeRankEmbed's hparams with the converter's own loader (`ModelBase.load_hparams`, read-only) returns zero moe/expert keys and `is_moe=False`.

### Affected versions

The offending line is byte-identical from release `b10068` through `b10076` (newest at time of writing, published 2026-07-21) and on current `master`. Per the commits API, `conversion/bert.py` was last touched by `bfb4308b` (2026-06-02) — before any of those releases — so every release in that span carries the unguarded lookup.

### Suggested fix

Either make the lookup optional:

```python
n_experts = self.find_hparam(["num_local_experts", "num_experts"], optional=True)
```

or move it inside the MoE tensor branches where it is actually consumed. (`nomic-bert-moe` models are unaffected either way.)

### How to reproduce

```
python convert_hf_to_gguf.py <local snapshot of nomic-ai/CodeRankEmbed> --outtype f16
# or any non-MoE NomicBert, e.g. nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1
```

diff --git a/conversion/bert.py b/conversion/bert.py
index 49a6948f6..0d25d0d62 100644
--- a/conversion/bert.py
+++ b/conversion/bert.py
@@ -369,12 +369,13 @@ class NomicBertModel(BertModel):
         return super().filter_tensors(item)
 
     def modify_tensors(self, data_torch: torch.Tensor, name: str, bid: int | None) -> Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]:
-        n_experts = self.find_hparam(["num_local_experts", "num_experts"])

[OpenCL] ggml_cl_flash_attn: is_causal heuristic incorrectly applies causal masking to ViT full attention, causing completely wrong vision output

## Environment

- **Device**: OnePlus Ace 5 (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, Adreno 750, Android 15)
- **llama.cpp commit**: `35c9b1f39`
- **Model**: Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct (Q4_0 LLM + F16 mmproj)
- **Backend**: OpenCL (`--mmproj-offload -ngl 99`)

## Bug

Running Qwen2.5-VL with the OpenCL backend, the mmproj (ViT visual encoder) produces **completely wrong** visual tokens regardless of the input image. The CPU path is correct; the OpenCL path is functionally broken.

Given a Termux terminal screenshot containing `pkg install` / `pkg search` commands:

| Path | Output | `pkg` token probability |
|---|---|---|
| CPU mmproj (`--no-mmproj-offload`) | correctly identifies `pkg search <query>`, `pkg install <package>` | **89.3%** |
| OpenCL mmproj (`--mmproj-offload`) | hallucinates a Windows file path `C:\Users\...\Main.java` | **6.9%** |

This is not a precision issue — it is a functional failure. The model cannot see the image at all.

## Root Cause

`ggml-opencl.cpp` is the **general-purpose OpenCL GPU backend** for GGML, shared by both LLM and ViT computations. Both call the same `ggml_cl_flash_attn()` function.

The bug is at **line 10889** of `ggml-opencl.cpp`, inside `ggml_cl_flash_attn()`:

```c
const int is_causal = (mask == NULL && n_q > 1 && n_q == n_kv);
```

This heuristic tries to detect LLM causal self-attention by shape alone, but it **incorrectly fires for ViT full-attention layers**:

- ViT full-attention passes `kq_mask = nullptr` — no explicit mask is needed for bidirectional attention
- ViT has `n_q == n_kv == n_patches` (e.g. 576 patches for a 336×336 image)
- `n_q > 1` is always true

All three conditions are satisfied → `is_causal = 1` → the kernel masks out all key positions `k > query_pos` with `-INFINITY`. This converts ViT's **bidirectional** self-attention into **causal** (unidirectional) attention: patch 0 can only attend to itself, patch 575 is the only one with full context. Global semantic aggregation is destroyed across all full-attention layers (6 out of 28 layers in Qwen2.5-VL-3B), and the error compounds through every subsequent layer.

**Why LLM is unaffected:** In the flash attention kernel, `is_causal` and the explicit `mask` tensor are **two independent code paths**. llama.cpp's LLM prefill always constructs and passes an explicit lower-triangular causal mask tensor (`mask != NULL`), so it goes through the mask tensor path and never relies on `is_causal`. During decode, `n_q = 1` fails the `n_q > 1` check.

**Why the CPU is correct:** The CPU flash_attn implementation (`ops.cpp`) has no such heuristic. When `mask = NULL`, it applies no masking at all (`mv = 0.0f` for all keys), giving correct bidirectional attention.

**Why this heuristic is effectively dead code for LLM:** The `ggml_flash_attn_ext` API has no `is_causal` parameter — per the API contract, callers that need causal attention must pass an explicit mask tensor. The heuristic is therefore an undocumented addition that contradicts the API design, and since LLM always provides an explicit mask, `is_causal` never equals 1 in the LLM path in practice.

## Fix

```diff
// ggml-opencl.cpp:10889
- const int is_causal = (mask == NULL && n_q > 1 && n_q == n_kv);
+ // ggml_flash_attn_ext has no is_causal parameter: callers that need causal
+ // attention must pass an explicit mask tensor. The heuristic above incorrectly
+ // fires for ViT full-attention (mask=NULL, n_q==n_kv==n_patches), converting
+ // bidirectional self-attention into causal and corrupting all vision output.
+ // LLM prefill always supplies an explicit mask, so this change is safe and
+ // aligns the OpenCL backend with the CPU implementation behavior.
+ const int is_causal = 0;
```

Verified on device: after this fix, OpenCL mmproj output matches CPU mmproj output correctly (`pkg` token probability recovers to ~89%).

version = 1

To add context to this issue, removing the `version` key, as @naumf recommends, shown in the example of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tree/master/tools/server#model-presets corrects this behavior and shouldn't cause any issues as its just skipped over:

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b97ebdc98f6053604a19d861c08d8087601b96e0/common/preset.cpp#L323-L326

Whether or not this is a bug would be up to @ngxson's original intentions in #17859.

The behavior comes from the `load_from_ini()` function:

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b97ebdc98f6053604a19d861c08d8087601b96e0/common/preset.cpp#L310-L360

As part of parsing the INI-style file, the function must assume a first section, which, if not yet defined, becomes `COMMON_PRESET_DEFAULT_NAME="default"` from `common/preset.h`. Then, it assigns the key-value pairs in the section, skipping the `version` key as mentioned above. After going through all the key-value pairs in the section, it creates a new mapping of the section name and key-value pairs, which if only including the `version` key as shown in the example from the llama-server documentation results in an empty "default" mapping.

This "default" section, which isn't mentioned in the documentation, is notably separate from the global "*" section, which is mentioned in https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tree/master/tools/server#model-presets. I believe both are necessary as they serve unique functions.

If this isn't the intended behavior, there are plenty of ways to correct it. Such as, adding a check if `preset.name == "default"`, same as done for "*" on L351 above. Then either just skip it, store it for later, or don't publish it at the `/models` endpoint.

If it is the intended behavior, possibly just mention it in the documentation at: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tree/master/tools/server#model-presets

The fit process only tries to offload different number of layers. It shouldn't be the root cause. Likely you can reproduce the same problem with `-ngl 39 -fit off`.

Most likely the CUDA backend decides to offload an op based on this logic:

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/635cdd5fcc5bdeb8ec2e108bb2a40acf62d9039b/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu#L5137-L5156

Maybe `ROPE_BACK`? And from there the FA is also offloaded.

---

Additionally, looking at the DSV4 graph, it is doing view operations with the weights. For example:

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/635cdd5fcc5bdeb8ec2e108bb2a40acf62d9039b/src/models/deepseek4.cpp#L1081

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/635cdd5fcc5bdeb8ec2e108bb2a40acf62d9039b/src/models/deepseek4.cpp#L285-L286

This does not play well with the "tensor info" logic here:

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/635cdd5fcc5bdeb8ec2e108bb2a40acf62d9039b/src/llama-arch.cpp#L609-L621

Generally, a weight should be used directly as it is loaded, without reshaping or viewing it. I recommend to fix that for DSV4 or we will keep seeing such problems like this issue. The fix would require updating the convert process to shape the weights in the right dimensions and using them directly, as declared in the "tensor info" section.

When running `convert_hf_to_gguf.py --mmproj` on Qwen2.5-Omni models, the output has only 1 tensor (7.7MB) instead of ~1008 tensors (2.6GB), causing model loading to fail.

**Root cause**: `Qwen25OmniModel.filter_tensors()` in `conversion/qwenvl.py` incorrectly filters tensors - the prefix check happens after `thinker.` replacement, excluding valid vision/audio tensors.

**Fix**: Reorder the prefix check in `filter_tensors()`.

Did some research, the tensor in question is:

```
(gdb) print(*node)
$9 = {type = GGML_TYPE_Q8_0, buffer = 0x0, ne = {768, 512, 1, 4}, nb = {544, 34, 544, 417792}, op = GGML_OP_NONE, 
  op_params = {0 <repeats 16 times>}, flags = 0, src = {0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0}, 
  view_src = 0x0, view_offs = 0, data = 0x0, 
  name = "CUDA0#cache_k_l0 (view) (permuted) (transposed)#0", '\000' <repeats 14 times>, extra = 0x0, 
  padding = "\000\000\000\000\000\000\000"}
```

which is transposed because of:

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/86a9c79f866799eb0e7e89c03578ccfbcc5d808e/src/llama-graph.cpp#L2488-L2492

@jettoblack does it happen if you enable flash attention in the command line? (`-fa on`)

@am17an So this was the reason you had changes increasing KV cache pad size to `MATRIX_ROW_PADDING` in your quantization support PR:

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/86a9c79f866799eb0e7e89c03578ccfbcc5d808e/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu#L914-L919

Here's the full mechanism of the issue:

1. Flash attention parameter is not set in the command line, so it's the default auto and at the same time V cache quantization is enabled,
2. The fit mechanism does its iterations, each time probing fused FA OP support,
3. At some point the probe fails due to whatever reason and FA is set to disabled,
4. Model graph is allocated with FA disabled and V quantization enabled,
5. Since V in DeepSeek V4 is simply K so it's not transposed, `llm_graph_context::build_attn_mha()` tries to do `v = ggml_cont(ctx0, ggml_transpose(ctx0, v))`
6. CUDA backend tries to allocate memory for `ggml_cont()` graph node and it triggers the assertion due to src0 tensor being transposed (see msg above).

When FA is explicitly disabled in the command line the crash does not happen as there is a check causing early failure.
When it's explicitly enabled the crash does not happen because there's no need to transpose V.

Converting Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507 (HF format, has tekken.json but no tokenizer.json) with plain `python convert_hf_to_gguf.py models/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507 --outfile out.gguf --outtype q8_0` dies with:

    vocab_size = self.hparams.get("vocab_size", len(tokenizer.vocab))
AttributeError: 'MistralCommonTokenizer' object has no attribute 'vocab'
```

The tekken branch in `LlamaModel.set_vocab` (conversion/llama.py, ~line 108) is missing a `return`:

```python
        if self.is_mistral_format:
            return self._set_vocab_mistral()

        path_tekken_json = self.dir_model / "tekken.json"
        path_tokenizer_json = self.dir_model / "tokenizer.json"
        if path_tekken_json.is_file() and not path_tokenizer_json.is_file():
            self._set_vocab_mistral()      # <- falls through
```

so after the mistral vocab is written successfully, it continues into the sentencepiece → llama_hf → gpt2 ladder and gpt2 chokes on the MistralCommonTokenizer wrapper. The `is_mistral_format` branch right above does return, and `conversion/mistral.py` has nothing after its `_set_vocab_mistral()` call either, so the fall-through looks like an oversight (it's been there since #14737 and survived the #17114 file split). Python GGUF parser (gguf_reader.py) lacks dimension validation present in C++ parser — DoS / crash on malicious model files

## Summary

The Python GGUF reader (`gguf-py/gguf/gguf_reader.py`) is missing input validation that exists in the C++ parser, making it vulnerable to DoS and crashes from crafted model files.

## Bug 1 — Missing `n_dims` upper bound (`gguf_reader.py` ~L267–271)

In `_get_tensor_info_field`, `n_dims` is read as `uint32` with **no upper-bound check against `GGML_MAX_DIMS` (4)**, unlike the C++ parser:

```python
n_dims = self._get(offs, np.uint32)
...
dims = self._get(offs, np.uint64, n_dims[0])
```

- A crafted file with `n_dims = 1000000` triggers an 8 MB read from the memmap (1000000 × 8 bytes), likely causing an `IndexError` crash when the file is too small — or hanging the process on large sparse files.
- `n_dims = 0xFFFFFFFF` would attempt a ~32 GiB allocation (via the memmap view), causing an OOM kill on most systems.

The C++ parser (`llama.cpp` in `llama_model_loader`) **does** clamp `n_dims` to `GGML_MAX_DIMS` before proceeding. The Python path lacks this guard entirely.

## Bug 2 — Integer overflow in `np.prod()` (`gguf_reader.py` ~L329–340)

In `_build_tensors`, total element count is computed as:

```python
n_elems = int(np.prod(dims))
```

`dims` is of type `np.uint64`, so `np.prod` wraps silently on overflow (modulo 2^64).

**Example:** `dims = [4194305, 4194305, 211106198978564]`
Actual product ≈ 3.7 × 10^27, but `np.prod` returns **4** due to wraparound.

This causes:
- An undersized `memmap` read (`item_count` is far too small)
- A subsequent `reshape(np_dims)` crash because the total element count doesn't match the shape

An attacker can craft a GGUF file that passes through the parser, triggers the overflow, and crashes any tool using the Python reader (e.g. `convert.py`, `scripts/`, or third-party GGUF consumers).

---

Both were reported to huntr.com (Protect AI's AI/ML bug bounty platform) and are awaiting validation. Flagging here directly since the Python parser is a separate implementation from the already-patched C++ parser (CVE-2026-33298), which does not cover this code path.

**Can a maintainer confirm these are still present and unaddressed?**

Eval bug: deepseek4 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) GGML_ASSERT abort in build_attention_impl with speculative decoding after #26531 (wo_a load-time reshape)

### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 1 (1269cb1)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

Built from tag `b10259` (= commit `1269cb1f`), CUDA 12.8.1, `CUDA_DOCKER_ARCH=61`.

Last known-good: `b10247` (= `dbadb68e`). The same model, same GGUF, same config loads and runs fine there.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

2x NVIDIA Quadro P5000 (Pascal, sm_61), 40-core dual-socket Xeon, 192 GB DDR4.
Experts on CPU (`--n-cpu-moe 43`), attention/KV on GPU.

### Models

`unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF`, UD-Q8_K_XL (5-part split), arch `deepseek4`.

Relevant metadata from the GGUF:

```
deepseek4.block_count                     43
deepseek4.embedding_length                4096
deepseek4.attention.head_count            64
deepseek4.attention.head_count_kv         1
deepseek4.attention.key_length            512
deepseek4.attention.value_length          512
deepseek4.attention.q_lora_rank           1024
deepseek4.attention.output_lora_rank      1024
deepseek4.attention.output_group_count    8
```

### Problem description

**`1269cb1f` ("model : allow reshape of tensors during load", #26531) makes DeepSeek-V4-Flash fail to load with a `GGML_ASSERT` abort.** This is a regression introduced by that commit — `b10247` (five commits earlier) loads and runs the identical model/config without issue.

The commit pre-reshapes `wo_a` to 3D at load time via the new `TENSOR_ALLOW_RESHAPE` flag and removes the corresponding `ggml_reshape_3d` from the graph:

`src/models/deepseek4.cpp:119`
```cpp
// for wo_a, the shape in the file is (n_head * n_embd_head / o_groups, o_lora_rank*o_groups)
// so we reshape here, to avoid reshaping the tensor in the graph
layer.wo_a = create_tensor(tn(LLM_TENSOR_ATTN_OUT_A, "weight", i),
        {n_head * n_embd_head / o_groups, o_lora_rank, o_groups}, flags | TENSOR_ALLOW_RESHAPE);
```

`src/models/deepseek4.cpp:1263` (graph side, reshape removed)
```cpp
ggml_tensor * oa = ggml_mul_mat(ctx0, layer.wo_a, out);
```

Previously this read:
```cpp
ggml_tensor * oa = ggml_mul_mat(ctx0,
        ggml_reshape_3d(ctx0, layer.wo_a, layer.wo_a->ne[0], o_lora_rank, n_groups), out);
```

Note the old graph-side reshape used `n_groups`, while the new load-time reshape uses `o_groups`. If those are not equal for this model, the pre-reshaped tensor has the wrong per-dimension layout even though the total element count is unchanged — which matches the observed failure, since the abort comes from the graph builder rather than from tensor creation.

For this model the total element count does work out the same either way:

```
n_head*n_embd_head/o_groups = 64*512/8 = 4096
4096 * 1024 * 8 = 33,554,432   (3D request)
4096 * 8192     = 33,554,432   (2D file shape per the comment)
```

so the assert is about dimension *arrangement*, not size.

### Relevant log output

```
common_speculative_init_result: loading draft model '/models/DeepseekV4-Flash-20260731-DSpark.gguf'
/app/ggml/src/ggml.c:3614: GGML_ASSERT(ggml_nelements(a) == (ne0*ne1*ne2*ne3)) failed
/app/libggml-base.so.0(ggml_abort+0x15b)[0x7f358e81d89b]
/app/libllama.so.0(_ZNK21llama_model_deepseek45graph20build_attention_implERK11llama_modelP20llm_graph_input_dsv4P27llm_graph_input_attn_k_iswaP11ggml_tensorS9_i+0x80a)[0x7f358eb2a92a]
/app/libllama.so.0(_ZNK21llama_model_deepseek45graph15build_attentionERK11llama_modelP27llm_graph_input_attn_k_iswaP11ggml_tensorS7_i+0x1a)[0x7f358eb2be0a]
srv    operator(): instance name=deepseek-v4-flash-284b exited with status 1
srv    operator(): got exception: {"error":{"code":500,"message":"model name=deepseek-v4-flash-284b failed to load","type":"server_error"}}
```

Demangled frames:
- `llama_model_deepseek4::graph::build_attention_impl(llama_model const&, llm_graph_input_dsv4*, llm_graph_input_attn_k_iswa*, ggml_tensor*, ggml_tensor*, int)`
- `llama_model_deepseek4::graph::build_attention(...)`

The abort is at `ggml.c:3614`, i.e. inside a reshape performed while building the attention graph, downstream of the pre-reshaped `wo_a`.

### Additional notes

- Reproduced deterministically: the model fails to load every time on `b10259`, and works every time on `b10247`.
- **The crash requires speculative decoding.** Isolated on the same b10259 binary: a section using the *same* Q8_K_XL GGUF and the same flags but with `--spec-type`/`--model-draft` removed **loads and generates normally** (`"Hello! How can I"`). Only the DSpark section aborts. So `wo_a` is fine in the ordinary graph and the mismatch appears on the speculative path — worth checking whether the draft/verify graph builds attention with a different `n_groups`/batch shape than the pre-reshape assumes.
- `--flash-attn on`, `--cache-type-k q8_0`, `--cache-type-v q8_0` (identical K/V types, so the `deepseek4` K==V check passes).
- Happy to test a patch or provide additional logs / tensor dumps.

### Name and Version

build: 74ce15741 (10335)
Built with Android NDK 30.0.15729638, arm64-v8a, ANDROID_PLATFORM=android-31.
Device: aarch64, 8 cores:
cpu0-5: 6x Cortex-A55
cpu6-7: 2x Cortex-A75
Operating system: Android

### Operating systems

Other? (Please let us know in description)

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

Other (Please specify in the next section), llama-bench

### Command line

```shell
# the run that ignores the mask (0xC0 = cpu6-7 on this device)
./llama-bench -m model.gguf -t 2 -C 0xC0 --cpu-strict 1 -r 3 -n 256 -p 0

# same binary pinned externally instead, for comparison
taskset c0 ./llama-bench -m model.gguf -t 2 -r 3 -n 128 -p 0
taskset 03 ./llama-bench -m model.gguf -t 2 -r 3 -n 128 -p 0
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Problem description & steps to reproduce

When compiling and running llama.cpp on Android, the CPU affinity mask (`-C`), which controls the logical CPU cores that each llama.cpp worker thread is allowed to run on, is accepted without returning any error, but the affinity is not actually applied at runtime.

`--cpu-strict` is affected the same way, since it goes through the same code path. Compilation succeeds; this is purely a runtime issue.

The affinity code is in `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c` (`ggml_thread_apply_affinity`), reached from `llama-bench` and `llama-cli` via `-C`.

My device has 8 cores: 6x Cortex-A55 on `cpu0-5` and 2x Cortex-A75 on `cpu6-7`. So `-C 0xC0` requests the two big cores.

### 1. Build for Android

```bash
cmake -B build-android \
  -D CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=$ANDROID_NDK_ROOT/build/cmake/android.toolchain.cmake \
  -D ANDROID_ABI=arm64-v8a \
  -D ANDROID_PLATFORM=android-31 \
  -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -D GGML_CPU_ARM_ARCH=armv8.2-a+fp16+dotprod \
  -D GGML_OPENMP=OFF

cmake --build build-android --target llama-bench -j
````

### 2. Push the binary, libraries, and model

```bash
adb shell mkdir -p /data/local/tmp/t
adb push build-android/bin/. /data/local/tmp/t/
adb push model.gguf /data/local/tmp/t/
adb shell chmod +x /data/local/tmp/t/llama-bench
```

### 3. Run with a restrictive affinity mask and inspect per-thread affinity

```bash
adb shell '
cd /data/local/tmp/t
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=. ./llama-bench -m model.gguf -t 2 -C 0xC0 --cpu-strict 1 -r 3 -n 256 -p 0 >/dev/null 2>&1 &
PID=$!
sleep 10
for t in /proc/$PID/task/*; do
    grep Cpus_allowed_list $t/status
done
wait $PID'
```

### Expected behavior

With `-C 0xC0 --cpu-strict 1`, each of the two worker threads should be pinned to one of the requested cores, so `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/status` should report `6` for one thread and `7` for the other.

### Actual behavior

Both threads report `0-7`. Nothing is written to stderr and the process exits with status `0`, so there is no indication that the requested affinity was dropped.

### Additional evidence

This does not appear to be Android refusing to set CPU affinity. The same binary pins correctly when placed externally with `taskset`, which also shows the expected ~2x throughput difference between the two core types.

Changing llama.cpp's own `-C` mask across those same two core groups moves throughput by less than the run-to-run error, with `-t 2` held constant and the runs interleaved. Commands and output are in the log output section below.

Eval bug: grammar : Unexpected empty grammar stack when trigger matches inside a longer word (e.g. "function" in "functional")

### Name and Version

./llama-cli --version
version: 10327 (69bf64379)
built with GNU 11.4.0 for Linux x86_64


### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

2x  ARC A770

### Models

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B/Qwen3.6-27B

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

 The server intermittently fails tool-call requests with:                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                            
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                                        
   got exception: Unexpected empty grammar stack after accepting piece: functional (47573)            
 ```                                               

 The whole request is aborted: the server sends an error to the client and releases the slot. The failure happens with --jinja enabled and a request that includes tools (i.e. the lazy tool-call grammar   
 generated from the chat template is active). It is intermittent because it depends on the model output: whenever the generated text contains a word that starts with the trigger word (e.g. the trigger    
 function matching inside functional), the grammar is activated at the wrong position and the request crashes.                                                                                              

 Root cause (from the code):                       

 1. llama_grammar_trigger_pattern::find() uses std::regex_search over the whole buffered output, so a trigger pattern fires when it matches anywhere in the buffer, not necessarily at a tool-call          
    boundary.                                      
 2. When the trigger fires, llama_grammar_accept_impl() replays the buffered token pieces into the grammar without any prior llama_grammar_apply_impl() validation. If the replayed text does not match the 
    grammar root (e.g. the trigger matched inside ordinary text), all grammar stacks die and llama_grammar_accept_token() throws std::runtime_error("Unexpected empty grammar stack after accepting piece:  
    ...").                                         
 3. The exception propagates up to server_context_impl::iterate() which catches it, returns an error to the client, and releases the slot, aborting the generation.                                         

 Steps to reproduce:                               

 1. Start the server with --jinja and a chat model whose template supports tool calls:                
    ```                                            
      llama-server -m model.gguf --jinja ...       
    ```                                            
 2. Send a chat request that includes tools (e.g. a single function definition) so that the lazy tool-call grammar with triggers is set up.                                                                 
 3. Make the model output a sentence containing a word that begins with the trigger string (e.g. trigger <tool_call> is safe, but trigger function matches inside functional; per-tool-name triggers such   
    as <function= can also match inside ordinary words).                                              
 4. Observe the error above and the aborted request.                                                  

 Expected behavior: the request should not be aborted; a spurious trigger should either not activate the grammar or degrade gracefully (e.g. continue unconstrained).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Summary

The UMA (Unified Memory Architecture) detection introduced in PR #17368 incorrectly identifies AMD APUs (such as Strix Halo) as UMA systems and limits the available GPU memory to system RAM's `MemAvailable`, ignoring the much larger TTM (Translation Table Manager) memory allocation that AMD APUs can utilize.

## Environment

- **Hardware**: AMD Strix Halo APU (gfx1151)
- **GPU Memory**: 96GB TTM allocation via kernel boot parameters
- **System RAM**: 32GB
- **OS**: Ubuntu Linux with kernel 6.14.0
- **ROCm Version**: 7.9.0
- **llama.cpp Version**: Latest master (commit 0a0bba05e)

### Kernel Boot Parameters
```
amdgpu.gttsize=98304 ttm.pages_limit=25000000 ttm.page_pool_size=12000000
```

## Problem Description

After PR #17368 (DGX Spark: UMA support), the `ggml_backend_cuda_device_get_memory()` function checks `prop.integrated > 0` to detect UMA systems. When detected as UMA, it reads available memory from `/proc/meminfo` instead of using `cudaMemGetInfo()`.

**The issue**: AMD APUs report `integrated = true`, but they can utilize significantly more memory than system RAM through TTM. In my case:
- System RAM available: ~27GB
- Actual GPU memory available via TTM: **96GB**

This causes the new `llama_params_fit` auto-fitting logic to incorrectly calculate that there isn't enough memory, resulting in:
1. Context size being reduced from 131072 to 4096
2. Model layers being offloaded to CPU unnecessarily
3. Significant performance degradation

## Logs

### Before patch (incorrect behavior):
```
llama_params_fit_impl: projected to use 64909 MiB of device memory vs. 98304 MiB of free device memory
llama_params_fit_impl: cannot fulfill margin of 1024 MiB, need to reduce device memory by 37767 MiB
llama_params_fit_impl: context size reduced from 131072 to 4096
llama_params_fit_impl: ROCm0 (AMD Radeon Graphics): 36 layers (21 overflowing), 27049 MiB used
```

### After patch (correct behavior):
```
llama_params_fit_impl: projected to use 64909 MiB of device memory vs. 98304 MiB of free device memory
llama_params_fit_impl: will leave 33092 >= 1024 MiB of free device memory, no changes needed
```

## Root Cause

In `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu`, the `ggml_backend_cuda_device_get_memory()` function:

```cpp
#if defined(__linux__)
    cudaDeviceProp prop;
    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceProperties(&prop, ctx->device));

    bool uma_env = getenv("GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY") != nullptr;
    bool is_uma = prop.integrated > 0 || uma_env;  // <-- AMD APUs hit this

    if (is_uma) {
        // Uses /proc/meminfo which returns ~27GB instead of 96GB TTM
        if (ggml_backend_cuda_get_available_uma_memory(&available_memory_kb, &free_swap_kb) && available_memory_kb > 0) {
            *free = (size_t)available_memory_kb * 1024;
        }
    }
#endif
```

## Proposed Fix

Skip the UMA memory detection for ROCm/HIP builds, as AMD APUs with TTM can report accurate memory via `hipMemGetInfo()`:

```diff
-#if defined(__linux__)
+#if defined(__linux__) && !defined(GGML_USE_HIP)
     // Check if this is a UMA (Unified Memory Architecture) system
+    // Note: Skip this for ROCm/HIP - AMD APUs with large TTM allocations (e.g., Strix Halo)
+    // report integrated=true but can use much more memory via TTM than system RAM
     cudaDeviceProp prop;
     CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceProperties(&prop, ctx->device));
     ...
-#endif // defined(__linux__)
+#endif // defined(__linux__) && !defined(GGML_USE_HIP)
```

## Alternative Solutions

1. **Environment variable override**: Add an env var like `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_UMA_DETECTION` to skip UMA detection
2. **TTM-aware detection for AMD**: Check `/sys/class/drm/card*/device/mem_info_vram_total` or similar for AMD GPUs
3. **Compare reported vs actual**: If `cudaMemGetInfo` returns significantly more than `MemAvailable`, prefer `cudaMemGetInfo`

## Verification

With the proposed patch applied:
- `amd-smi` shows 65GB+ GPU memory usage (correct)
- Model loads with full 128K context
- All 36 layers stay on GPU
- No unnecessary CPU offloading

## Related

- PR #17368: DGX Spark: UMA support
- PR #17537: cuda: fix UMA detection on discrete GPUs

**Config:** Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 128 GB RAM, **96 GB dedicated VRAM carveout set in BIOS** (not a kernel TTM param), so the OS sees ~30 GB RAM. ROCm 7.2.4. **Concern with `&& !defined(GGML_USE_HIP)`:** that disables the UMA path for *all* HIP builds, which would re-break genuinely shared-memory HIP APUs (small-carveout iGPUs) that this override was added for. It fixes dedicated-carveout APUs by removing the feature for the shared ones.

**Alternative that handles both:** take the **max** of the two values instead of overwriting — never lower the driver-reported VRAM below what `hipMemGetInfo` already returned:

```cpp
if (ggml_backend_cuda_get_available_uma_memory(&available_memory_kb, &free_swap_kb) && available_memory_kb > 0) {
    const size_t uma_free = (size_t)available_memory_kb * 1024;
    if (uma_free > *free) {   // only raise to system RAM, never clobber real VRAM
        *free = uma_free;
    }
}
```

- Dedicated carveout: `hipMemGetInfo` free (~95 GB) > system RAM (~27 GB) → keep ~95 GB.
- True shared APU: `hipMemGetInfo` free (small heap) < system RAM → use system RAM (current behavior preserved).

```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When a single user message contains two adjacent image_url content parts whose
images have identical pixel dimensions, the second image is silently discarded.
The prompt is built as if only one image had been supplied.

The discriminator is the pixel dimensions, not the content: two completely unrelated
images merge as long as width x height matches. Images of different dimensions are
both kept. Inserting any text content part between the two images also prevents the
merge, which is a usable workaround.

There is no warning and no error — the request succeeds and the model answers
confidently from the truncated input. usage.prompt_tokens is the objective evidence:
it stays at the single-image value.

The reproduction below is self-contained: it generates its own PNGs (two 448x448 images
with a black square on the left / on the right, plus one 336x336 control) and needs
nothing beyond the standard library.

python3 repro.py http://localhost:8080 [api-key]



repro.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal reproduction: llama-server drops the 2nd of two adjacent images
that have identical pixel dimensions.

    python3 repro.py http://localhost:8080 [api-key]

Generates its own images, no dependencies beyond the standard library.
"""
import base64, json, struct, sys, urllib.request, zlib

BASE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://localhost:8080"
KEY = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else ""

def png(path, w, h, inside):
    rows = []
    for y in range(h):
        row = bytearray(b"\x00")
        for x in range(w):
            row += b"\x00\x00\x00" if inside(x, y) else b"\xff\xff\xff"
        rows.append(bytes(row))
    def chunk(t, d):
        c = t + d
        return struct.pack(">I", len(d)) + c + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(c) & 0xffffffff)
    open(path, "wb").write(
        b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
        + chunk(b"IHDR", struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0))
        + chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(b"".join(rows), 9))
        + chunk(b"IEND", b""))

# Same dimensions, different content. Third image: different dimensions.
png("left.png",  448, 448, lambda x, y:  40 < x < 200 and 140 < y < 300)
png("right.png", 448, 448, lambda x, y: 248 < x < 408 and 140 < y < 300)
png("small.png", 336, 336, lambda x, y:  40 < x < 160 and 100 < y < 220)

def img(f):
    b64 = base64.b64encode(open(f, "rb").read()).decode()
    return {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64," + b64}}

def txt(s):
    return {"type": "text", "text": s}

Q = txt("For each image you are shown, say whether the black square is on the "
        "LEFT or the RIGHT. Answer one word per image, in order.")

CASES = [
    ("1 image                       ", [img("left.png"), Q]),
    ("1 image                       ", [img("right.png"), Q]),
    ("2 images, SAME dimensions     ", [img("left.png"), img("right.png"), Q]),
    ("2 images, SAME dimensions, rev", [img("right.png"), img("left.png"), Q]),
    ("2 images, text part between   ", [img("left.png"), txt("next image:"), img("right.png"), Q]),
    ("2 images, DIFFERENT dimensions", [img("left.png"), img("small.png"), Q]),
]

for label, content in CASES:
    body = json.dumps({"model": "x", "max_tokens": 20, "temperature": 0,
                       "cache_prompt": False,
                       "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    if KEY:
        headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer " + KEY
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + "/v1/chat/completions", data=body, headers=headers)
    j = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=900).read().decode())
    print("%s  prompt_tokens=%4d  -> %r" % (label, j["usage"]["prompt_tokens"],
                                            j["choices"][0]["message"]["content"].strip()))

Longer runs of same-sized images are collapsed pairwise rather than entirely: three

Eval bug: CUDA "unsupported value" in cublasSgemm (mul_mat_cublas) after ~2500 decoded tokens with DSpark speculative decoding (deepseek4, multi-GPU)

### Summary

With DSpark speculative decoding (`--spec-type draft-dspark`) on DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, llama-server reliably aborts with a CUDA error after roughly **2,000–2,600 decoded tokens** in a single response. Three crashes over two days, all with the same signature; short responses never crash. Reproduced on **b10242 and b10257**.

### Error

```
/home/mp/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu:106: CUDA error
E CUDA error: an unsupported value or parameter was passed to the function
E   current device: 0, in function ggml_cuda_mul_mat_cublas_impl at /home/mp/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu:1541
E   cublasSgemm_v2(ctx.cublas_handle(), CUBLAS_OP_T, CUBLAS_OP_N, ne01, ne11, ne10, (const float *) alpha, (const float *) src0_ptr, s01, (const float *) src1_ptr, s11, (const float *) beta, (float *) dst_ptr, ne0)
```

Last server log line before the abort (crash #3):

```
I slot print_timing: id  0 | task 7 | n_decoded =   2518, tg =  20.42 t/s, tg_3s =  21.22 t/s
```

### Pattern

| Crash | Build | Prompt tokens | Decoded before abort | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #1 | b10242 | ~11k | ~2,5–3k (est., 16.6 t/s × ~3 min) | long reasoning response |
| #2 | b10242 | ~4k | ~2–2.5k (est.) | long reasoning response |
| #3 | b10257 | ~4k | **2,518** (from `print_timing`) | long reasoning response |

- Only long, reasoning-heavy generations crash; code-heavy answers of a few hundred tokens are fine.
- An FP32 GEMM (`cublasSgemm_v2`) in the decode path looks unusual — suspicion: the DSpark markov head or the DeepSeek sparse-attention indexer produces a degenerate shape (a dim/stride of 0 or an ld below the cuBLAS minimum) once the sequence crosses some threshold.
- For comparison: Qwen MTP profiles (`--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3`, same machine, same multi-GPU setup) have never shown this crash. We are currently testing whether `--spec-draft-n-max 3` instead of 5 avoids it on DSpark, too.

### Setup

- Model: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` UD-Q4_K_XL (unsloth GGUF, 5 split files) + `dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf` sidecar
- GPUs: 2× Quadro RTX 8000 (48 GB) + 3× Tesla V100-PCIE-32GB, pinned via `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<uuid list>` (RTX first)
- Driver 580.173.02, CUDA runtime 13.0, built with nvcc 12.0, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=70;75`, Linux x86_64
- Command (crash #3, `${PORT}` filled in by llama-swap):

```
llama-server --port ${PORT} \
  --model .../DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00005.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -c 137728 -sm layer --tensor-split 12,12,6,8,5 -fit off \
  -b 2048 -ub 2048 --flash-attn on -np 1 -t 4 --mlock --direct-io \
  --jinja --reasoning-format deepseek --no-context-shift \
  --temp 1.0 --top-k 40 --top-p 1.0 --min-p 0.05 --repeat-penalty 1.0 \
  --model-draft .../dspark/dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-dspark --spec-draft-n-max 5 --gpu-layers-draft 99 \
  --device-draft CUDA4 --cache-reuse 256
```

(K/V cache f16; the draft sidecar is pinned to the device holding the main model's output layer — other placements abort at load with `pre-allocated tensor (output.weight) in a buffer (CUDA4) that cannot run the operation`.)

Happy to provide full logs, GDB backtraces or test patches — the crash is reproducible within minutes by asking for a long reasoning answer.

- Crash #4: after prompt processing of **26,695 tokens** (long session, ~350 t/s PP), abort at only **n_decoded = 180** (26.9 t/s until then). Same `cublasSgemm_v2` / "unsupported value or parameter" at ggml-cuda.cu:1541, device 0.

@0cc4m sorry to bump you, is it working on your hardware. I’m seeing a very similar issue on a dual Intel Arc Pro B60 setup using the llama.cpp `server-intel` Docker image with SYCL. The important detail is that `Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf` and `Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-Q6_K.gguf` both work cleanly on the same stack, across both GPUs. But `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf` and `Qwen3-Coder-Next-Q4_K_M.gguf` produce gibberish / random multilingual output even on simple prompts like `Hello?`. I tested with: ```bash --flash-attn off --cache-ram 0 --split-mode layer --tensor-split 1,1 -ngl 999 --batch-size 512 --ubatch-size 128 ``` The server loads the model, but generation is corrupt. Logs for Qwen3.6 show `thinking = 1` and repeated checkpoint invalidation due to hybrid/recurrent memory. This feels specific to Qwen3.6 / Coder-Next architecture or UD quant handling on GPU backends, not a general Intel Arc/SYCL setup problem, because Qwen3-Coder-30B Q4/Q6 work correctly.

Perf: CUDA: Mamba2 batched decode dispatch GEMV instead of GEMM

### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

With CUDA backend, I noticed that Nemotron 3 Nano (30B A3B NVFP4) model was decoding slower than alternate baseline inference engine with concurrency npl>=8. Profiling showed that it was launching `mul_mat_vec_*` instead of GEMM, and was dominating GPU time ~40% at npl=32. 

This was due to `mamba-base.cpp` reshaping activations to `{n_embd, n_seq_tokens, n_seqs}` before `ssm_in`/`ssm_out`. So with decode `n_seq_tokens==1` the dispatcher sees `ne11==1` and treats it as column-batched GEMV for what is a dense GEMM. See below:

```cpp
// mamba-base.cpp
// {n_embd, n_tokens} => {n_embd, n_seq_tokens, n_seqs}
cur = ggml_reshape_3d(ctx0, cur, cur->ne[0], n_seq_tokens, n_seqs);
```

```cpp
y = ggml_reshape_3d(ctx0, y, d_inner, n_seq_tokens, n_seqs);
```

### Motivation

I noticed that Nemotron 3 Nano (30B A3B) model was decoding slower than alternate baseline inference engine with concurrency npl>=8, digging deeper into it uncovered this issue. The proposed fix would signficantly improve decode rate for Mamba2 models especially at higher concurrency.

### Possible Implementation

This can be improved by keeping the tensor flat in 2d so the backend dispatches the more efficient GEMM which is numerically equivalent. I made the proposed change locally and did some perf benchmarking.

## Perf impact

Measured the performance impact of this change with relevant Mamba2 models with CUDA backend on GB10 (sm121) and RTX PRO 6000 (sm120). The results are shown below as text-generation tokens/s. The numbers are on master `78ec4c3` with `llama-batched-bench -npp 64 -ntg 128 -ngl 1,8,32,256`.

Trailing assistant message with tool_calls: calls silently dropped from rendered prompt (auto-prefill/continuation path)

## Description

When the last message of a `/v1/chat/completions` (or `/apply-template`) request is an **assistant message carrying `tool_calls`**, the tool calls are **silently dropped** from the rendered prompt. The assistant turn renders as an empty turn and the model is asked to continue from a prompt in which the pending tool calls no longer exist.

## Environment

- upstream master `2115b73`, Vulkan build, `llama-server` with `--jinja`
- model: Qwen3.8-27B GGUF (reproduced with both the embedded official Qwen3.8 chat template and a custom `--chat-template-file`)
- reproduced identically on a fork build pinned at `9b9ac3e38`

## Repro (no inference needed — `/apply-template`)

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/apply-template -d '{
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "weather?"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [
      {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Rome"}}}
    ]}
  ],
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {
    "name": "get_weather",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}
  }}],
  "add_generation_prompt": true
}'
```

Rendered tail (tool call gone, assistant turn empty):

```
<|im_start|>user\nweather?<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n\n</think>\n\n
```

Control — same conversation with a `role:"tool"` response appended — renders the call correctly (`<tool_call>\n<function=get_weather>...` appears exactly once).

## Root cause (as far as I traced)

`tools/server/server-common.cpp` (~line 1255): with prefill enabled (the default for `--prefill-assistant`), a trailing assistant message triggers `CONTINUATION_AUTO` and `add_generation_prompt` is forced off. The continuation prefill in `common/chat.cpp` (the `inputs.has_continuation()` blocks, e.g. ~line 1201) then builds the generation prompt from `msg.reasoning_content` + `msg.render_content()` only — **`msg.tool_calls` is never serialized**, so the call vanishes from the prompt.

## Expected behavior

Either
- include the serialized tool calls in the continuation prefill, or
- reject the request loudly (e.g. 400 "cannot prefill continuation of an assistant message with tool_calls") instead of silently corrupting the prompt.

Silent data loss is the worst option: the model continues after a tool-call turn whose calls no longer exist in its context.

## Impact

Any client that replays history ending in `assistant(tool_calls)` — agent frameworks storing pending tool calls between rounds, "continue/regenerate after tool call" flows — gets a corrupted prompt with no error anywhere.

Happy to turn this into a PR if the maintainers prefer a specific behavior (serialize vs. reject).

Nemotron 3.5 Lightning Q4_0: zero KV head metadata misclassifies Attention blocks as SSM

## Summary

I isolated a metadata inconsistency in the official `NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-Q4_0.gguf` artifact.

The affected GGUF contains Attention tensors for block 5:

* `blk.5.attn_k.weight`
* `blk.5.attn_q.weight`
* `blk.5.attn_v.weight`
* `blk.5.attn_output.weight`

It does not contain `blk.5.ssm_in.weight`.

However, its per layer `nemotron_h_moe.attention.head_count_kv` metadata is all zero. On the tested llama.cpp build, this causes block 5 to be interpreted as SSM and the loader attempts to resolve the nonexistent tensor `blk.5.ssm_in.weight`.

## Expected metadata

NVIDIA's model configuration declares `num_key_value_heads = 2` and identifies block 5 as an Attention layer.

The official ggml conversion log also first reports `key value head count = 2`, but later records a duplicate key overwrite of `nemotron_h_moe.attention.head_count_kv` with a 52 element all zero array.

## Reproduction environment

* GGUF: `NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-Q4_0.gguf`
* SHA256: `b1cc80f0bfa080612ac035cd54ddbe9c7c8283add596e7fe425445bfe4c5486f`
* llama.cpp: build 10626, commit `1729ed5371cd1ac6f6d6f3226f8803b080042839`
* OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4
* GPU: AMD Radeon 8060S, gfx1151
* ROCm: 7.2.53211-e1a6bc5663

## Causality test

I created a separate diagnostic copy and changed only the affected per layer KV head metadata. The original artifact was not modified.

The diagnostic copy successfully loaded and generated with:

1. CPU only execution
2. ROCm HIP partial GPU offload
3. ROCm HIP full GPU offload

This isolates the observed `blk.5.ssm_in.weight` failure to metadata driven Attention to SSM misclassification, rather than GPU memory capacity, Flash Attention, MTP, or ROCm offload in this test case.

## Requested guidance

Could maintainers confirm:

1. Whether the duplicate key overwrite is expected
2. Which component should preserve the correct per layer KV head values
3. Whether conversion or export should validate consistency among `layers_block_type`, `attention.head_count_kv`, `feed_forward_length`, and physical `attn_*` and `ssm_*` tensor namespaces before publishing

## Scope and limitations

This report concerns one official artifact identified by the SHA256 above. It does not claim that all Nemotron H GGUF files are affected, nor that ROCm has no independent Nemotron H or SSM limitations.

Technical report, raw observations, validation controls, and known good comparison artifact:

query:
Vulkan: wrong matmul results on Adreno (subgroupSize=128) — warptile WM exceeds BM (implicit `WM <= BM` invariant violated for subgroupSize > 64)

## Environment
- llama.cpp commit `bf2c86d` (also present in whisper.cpp's bundled ggml — its own tree must be patched too)
- Vulkan backend, **Adreno 650** via Mesa Turnip, `subgroupSize = 128` (double threadsize)
- Applies to **any device that reports `subgroupSize > 64`**, not just Adreno

## Symptom
`./test-backend-ops -b Vulkan0 -o MUL_MAT` — **2 of 229 f16 cases FAIL** with large error,
all of them **batched + broadcast + partial-tile** shapes:
```
MUL_MAT(type_a=f16,type_b=f32,m=64, n=45,k=128,bs=[8,1],nr=[4,1])  ERR = 0.414  FAIL
MUL_MAT(type_a=f16,type_b=f32,m=128,n=45,k=64, bs=[8,1],nr=[4,1])  ERR = 1.079  FAIL
```
Real workloads (whisper.cpp) produce **garbage / looping output** on the GPU while the
CPU backend on the same model is correct.

## Root cause
In `ggml_vk_load_shaders()` (`ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp`), warptiles are built
with **WM** (index 4) and **WARP** (index 10) = `subgroup_size_8 = max(device->subgroup_size, 8)`:
```cpp
l_warptile = { 128, 128, 128, 16, subgroup_size_8 * 2, 64, 2, ..., subgroup_size_8 }; // BM=128, WM=subgroup*2
m_warptile = { 128,  64,  64, 16, subgroup_size_8,     32, 2, ..., subgroup_size_8 }; // BM=64,  WM=subgroup
```
These encode an implicit invariant **`WM <= BM`**. It holds for
`subgroupSize ∈ {8,16,32,64}` but **breaks at 128**: `m_warptile` gets `WM = 128 > BM = 64`,
`l_warptile` gets `WM = 256 > BM = 128`.

In `mul_mm.comp` this detonates in three ways for the degenerate tile:
1. `BM / WM` folds to **0** (unsigned) → `warp_r = warp_i % (BM/WM)` / `warp_c = warp_i / (BM/WM)` are `udiv`/`umod` by zero.
2. `buf_a` shared-memory indexing addresses rows `0..WM-1`, but `buf_a` is only
   `BM * SHMEM_STRIDE` entries; for `WM > BM` it **runs past its end into `buf_b`**, so the
   `A` operands become `B` data.
3. Only the first `WN` of the `BN` output columns are ever written; columns `WN..BN-1` are
   **never computed/stored**.

The **small tile** (`s_warptile`) uses `BM = WM = subgroup_size_32` so it stays
self-consistent — which is exactly why **only medium/large tiles fail** (need `n > 32`
*and* `m > 32`); every *passing* case in the suite is a small-tile case.

## Fix (verified working)
Clamp the tiling WARP for the `l_`/`m_` warptiles to 64, **leaving `s_warptile` untouched**:
```cpp
const uint32_t subgroup_size_8 = std::max(device->subgroup_size, 8u);
const uint32_t mm_warp_8       = std::min(subgroup_size_8, 64u);           // NEW: l_/m_ warptiles only
const uint32_t mul_mat_mm_warp_8 = std::min(mul_mat_subgroup_size_8, 64u); // NEW: mmqid l_/m_ warptiles
```
then use `mm_warp_8` (resp. `mul_mat_mm_warp_8`) in every `l_warptile*` / `m_warptile*`
definition in place of `subgroup_size_8` (resp. `mul_mat_subgroup_size_8`) — 18 lines.

⚠️ **`s_warptile` must keep the unclamped value**: its `BLOCK_SIZE` is `subgroup_size_32`
and it needs `NUM_WARPS == 1` to keep its area at `BM*BN`. Clamping it too **regresses
`m=1` (matrix-vector)** — verified.

Result after the fix: **f16 229/229 and f32 173/173 pass**, whisper.cpp transcribes correctly.

## Note for maintainers
A cleaner central fix may be preferred (e.g. `assert(WM <= BM)` in the warptile builder and
select a valid tiling, or clamp `WM` to `BM` generically), but the scoped
`mm_warp_8 = min(subgroup_size_8, 64)` is minimal and verified. Since `NUM_WARPS*WM*WN ==
BM*BN` and `WM <= BM` both continue to hold for `l_`/`m_` after clamping, occupancy is
unaffected on subgroupSize ≤ 64 devices (the `min` is a no-op there).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

The llama-server does not allow using the extended context. Server output announces the context length is capped

> the slot context (%d) exceeds the training context of the model (%d) - capping\n

This is not aware of RoPE settings or other user configurations which would allow for longer context. Disabling this check in llama-server introduced in cd5e3b57 allowed me to use longer context via the RoPE settings.

This "capping" forces the model to load with 4,096 tokens of context and causes my long-context queries to fail.

Please allow us to override this cap. For users who don't know what they are doing, sure, it's probably helpful, but for advanced users there should be a way to disable it.

Eval bug: KleidiAI dotprod GEMV ~3x slower than CPU repack for token generation on Apple M1 Max (Q4_0), while winning on Neoverse N1/N2 — no runtime escape when both compiled in

### What happened

On Apple M1 Max (dotprod, no i8mm/SME), building with `-DGGML_CPU_KLEIDIAI=ON` makes token generation ~3x slower than the CPU repack path, while prefill stays comparable. The same binary configuration ranks the other way on Neoverse N2 and — surprisingly — on Neoverse N1 (Graviton2), which shares the M1's dotprod-only feature set, KleidiAI wins both axes. So the regression appears specific to M1-class cores rather than to the dotprod-only feature level in general.

Because the KleidiAI extra-buffer type outranks repack when both are compiled in (registration order in `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.cpp`), and `--no-repack` disables both paths together, an M1 user who builds with KleidiAI enabled cannot recover the fast generation path at runtime.

### Measurements (commit 74ce157)

Apple M1 Max, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 Q4_0, t=8, pp512/tg128, p50 of 5 reps:

| Build | prefill tok/s | gen tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| GGML_CPU_REPACK=ON, KLEIDIAI=OFF | 186.4 | **31.9** |
| GGML_CPU_KLEIDIAI=ON | 182.2 | **10.5** |

Also reproduces on Qwen3-0.6B Q4_0 on the same host (tg64 at t=8: ~31 vs ~202 tok/s — larger gap at the smaller model size).

Cross-checks, same builds, Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0, pp128/tg32 (quick protocol, ranking is the claim):

| Host | repack pp / tg | kleidiai pp / tg |
|---|---|---|
| Neoverse N2 (i8mm+SVE2, GitHub arm64 runner) | 153.0 / 55.3 | **232.5 / 60.8** |
| Neoverse N1 (dotprod-only, AWS Graviton2 t4g) | 135.9 / 45.1 | **228.6 / 49.4** |

Arm Performix `code_hotspots` profiles on the Graviton2 host confirm each build spends its self-time where expected (`ggml_gemm/gemv_q8_0_4x4_q8_0` vs `kai_run_matmul_*_neon_dotprod`), so this is kernel-path selection, not a build misconfiguration.

### Reproduction

Full harness, raw per-rep samples, and exact commands (every run records its verbatim command):
https://github.com/tjohnson012/whetstone — sessions in `results/sessions/`, protocol in `docs/METHODOLOGY.md`. The two-build A/B is:

```
cmake -B build-repack -DGGML_NATIVE=ON -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_CPU_KLEIDIAI=OFF -DGGML_METAL=OFF
cmake -B build-kleidi -DGGML_NATIVE=ON -DGGML_CPU_KLEIDIAI=ON -DGGML_METAL=OFF
build-*/bin/llama-bench -m Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-Q4_0.gguf -p 512 -n 128 -r 5 -t 8
```

### Possible directions

- Prefer repack GEMV over the KleidiAI dotprod GEMV on Apple Silicon (or benchmark-gate the choice at load), and/or
- make the extra-buffer-type priority runtime-configurable so `KLEIDIAI=ON` builds can still reach the repack path.

Related: #20386 (RK3588 slower with KleidiAI, closed) looks like the same class of issue on different silicon.

[Vulkan] FA f16-scratch fast path never enabled for hybrid-model (non-unified) KV caches

## Summary

On hybrid architectures (e.g. Qwen3.5/3.8 with DeltaNet/SSM layers), the Flash Attention
f16-scratch fast path (`use_dequant_kv`) is never enabled for quantized KV caches, because
`is_dense_kv_cache()` rejects the per-layer KV view. This makes prefill significantly slower
for all quantized KV types on these models.

## Environment

- llama.cpp master (2026-08-30), Vulkan backend
- AMD Radeon RX 9070 (RDNA4), Windows
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B (qwen35 arch, hybrid: 16 attention layers + SSM layers, non-unified KV)

## Root cause

`ggml_vk_flash_attn()` has this guard:

```cpp
auto is_dense_kv_cache = [](const ggml_tensor * t) {
    return t->nb[0] == ggml_type_size(t->type) &&
           t->nb[2] == ggml_row_size(t->type, t->ne[0]) &&
           t->nb[1] == t->nb[2] * t->ne[2] &&
           t->nb[3] == t->nb[1] * t->ne[1];   // never true for hybrid views
};
```

For hybrid models the KV cache is non-unified (`kv_unified=false`). `get_k()` returns a
view covering only `n_kv` cells:

```cpp
return ggml_view_4d(ctx, k,
        n_embd_head_k(il), n_head_kv(il), n_kv, ns,
        ggml_row_size(k->type, n_embd_head_k(il)),
        ggml_row_size(k->type, n_embd_k_gqa),
        ggml_row_size(k->type, n_embd_k_gqa * kv_size),   // full-cache stride
        ggml_row_size(k->type, n_embd_k_gqa * kv_size) * sinfo.s0);
```

So `nb[3]` is the **full-cache** stride (kv_size cells) while `ne[1]` is only `n_kv`
(used cells). The equality `nb[3] == nb[1]*ne[1]` never holds → `is_dense_kv_cache` false
→ f16-scratch fast path disabled for **all** quantized KV types on hybrid models.

## Measured impact (Qwen3.8-27B, 21.5K prompt)

| | before (fast path disabled) | after (fast path enabled) |
|---|---|---|
| prefill | 65 tok/s | **119 tok/s (+83%)** |
| needle-test correctness | exact | exact (ZX-73912) |
| decode | unchanged | unchanged |

## Question for maintainers

Is this guard intentionally conservative, or is it a bug for per-layer views of non-unified
caches? The view layout `[elem][head][token]` with full-cache `nb[3]` matches what
`DEQUANT_TRANSPOSE` expects, so it seems the fast path *should* apply.

A candidate fix (local, tested on Qwen3.8 only — **not** proposed as a PR yet):

```cpp
// Only single-stream views are accepted to keep the DEQUANT_TRANSPOSE remap valid.
auto is_dense_kv_cache = [](const ggml_tensor * t) {
    return t->ne[3] == 1 &&
           t->nb[0] == ggml_type_size(t->type) &&
           t->nb[2] == ggml_row_size(t->type, t->ne[0]) &&
           t->nb[1] == t->nb[2] * t->ne[2] &&
           t->nb[3] >= t->nb[1] * t->ne[1];   // relax: per-layer view spans n_kv of full buffer
};
```

Concerns before proposing as PR:
- Does `ne[3] == 1` fully guarantee the view is a single stream (safe for the remap)?
- Could `nb[3] >= nb[1]*ne[1]` wrongly accept a padded/non-contiguous view and cause
  silent wrong output on other hybrid models? (Only tested on Qwen3.8.)
- Is `use_dequant_kv` also gated elsewhere for multi-stream/hybrid cases?

Happy to turn this into a PR if maintainers confirm the direction. A debug aid
(`LLAMA_VK_FA_DEBUG=1` env prints the per-call decision) is available locally if useful.
